character.name: Pip
character.description: a small round clay gardener with a mustard knitted beanie, rosy cheeks, big expressive oval eyes, chunky clay hands with cracked dry knuckles shown as tiny fissures, olive overalls

shots.scene: Pip in a tiny frosty clay garden at dawn, holding a watering can, wincing as he flexes his cracked knuckles
shots.action: Pip flexes his fingers and winces, breath fogs
shots.vo: Winter knuckles. You know the ones.
shots.caption: Winter knuckles. You know the ones.

shots.scene: Pip at a cluttered clay potting bench trying three different lotion tubes that slide off his hands like slime
shots.action: a lotion blob slides off Pip's hand, he shrugs at the camera
shots.vo: Most lotions sit on top and slide off by lunch.
shots.caption: Most lotions slide off by lunch.

shots.scene: a small tin of balm with a plain sage-green label (no text) on the potting bench, morning light hitting it
shots.camera: macro product shot, slow push in
shots.action: the tin lid twists open by itself, revealing thick creamy balm
shots.vo: This one's a thick balm. A pea-sized bit, worked in.
shots.caption: A pea-sized bit, worked in.

shots.scene: Pip rubbing balm into his knuckles, the clay fissures smoothing out as he rubs
shots.action: Pip rubs his hands together, cracks smooth over, he wiggles his fingers happily
shots.vo: Gardeners say it's the first thing that actually stays put.
shots.caption: "The first thing that actually stays put."

shots.scene: Pip back in the frosty garden, now digging happily with bare hands
shots.action: Pip digs and gives a thumbs up to camera
shots.vo: Your hands, back on the job.
shots.caption: Back on the job.
